messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: multi-region healthcheck alert — us-east showing sustained 5xx + queue backlog. Severity: P1. service: inference-router. initial signal: failover monitor tripped at 1945689999.

rahul (oncall): ack. i'm on it. checking region metrics and routing table.

maya (sre): early signs: a burst of large-batch requests hitting encoder workers in us-east-1, memory pressure -> pod restarts. autoscaler is slow to react due to cooldown settings.

chris (prod-eng): last deploy? small change to encoder memory config rolled 2h ago but targeted staging. nothing scheduled for prod. could be a client workload spike.

nora (support): two customers reported degraded completions around the same time. ticket IDs attached. escalating to CS.

oliver (pm): pinging CS for context, will update customers if we route around.

rahul (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) enable regional failover to prefer eu-west for new sessions; 2) throttle large-batch requests via gateway --- apply temporary rate-limiter; 3) mute noisy non-actionable alerts while assessing root cause. executing now.

incident-bot: action logged 1A `routerctl apply policy failover --service inference-router --preference=eu-west,us-west --percent=40` by rahul (oncall) at 1945690012.

tara (monitoring): applying alert suppression window for `encoder_pod_oom` and `regional_5xx_spike` for 20m. creating a short-lived panel grouping per-region queue depth + routing percent.

maya (sre): temporarily scaling encoder replica set by +50% in us-east to relieve backlog: `kubectl scale deployment/encoder -n prod --replicas=9`

chris (prod-eng): adding a gateway throttle: `gatewayctl set-limits --service inference-gateway --max-batch-tokens 512 --max-concurrent 20` to protect encoders.

rahul (oncall): traffic shift visible: eu-west ingestion up 38% over baseline, us-east down by comparable amount. 5xx rate in affected customers dropped from 7.3% -> 1.1% after routing change.

nora (support): sending interim status to customers: "We've routed your traffic to a healthy region and applied throttles to large batches. You may see slightly different latency while we stabilize. We'll follow up with a timeline."

maya (sre): initial RCA hypothesis: client-side large-batch burst + encoder memory leak in a rarely exercised code path. Need logs from encoder pods and heap dumps from one of the restarters.

incident-bot: note: heapdump job scheduled by maya at 1945690230.

rahul (oncall): handoff prep: kim (next oncall) incoming at 1945690300. will leave routing policy in place at 40% for 30m, suppression until 20m from now. please monitor `regional_traffic_shift` and `encoder_restart_rate`.

kim (oncall): taking over. thanks rahul. i'll watch dashboards and keep alert suppression timeline.

tara (monitoring): follow-up alert tuning proposals (to be PR'd):
- new alert `regional_traffic_shift` (fires when >20% traffic moves between regions in <10m). severity: INFO. will not page immediately, only notify channel.
- adjust `encoder_pod_oom` threshold: increase anomaly baseline during known batch windows; add dynamic baseline based on request token distribution.
- add composite alert that suppresses compile/oom noise when `regional_traffic_shift` is active.

chris (prod-eng): +1 on composite suppression. also propose adding a canary gate to the encoder memory change paths so we don't hit prod-wide regressions.

maya (sre): opening issue to add autoscaler sensitivity tweak: consider restart_rate and queue_depth together before scaling decisions (PR #8901).

rahul (oncall): paging/handoff note: current status at 1945690450: routing fallback active (40% eu-west), encoder replicas scaled, throttle applied, suppression active. customers showing nominal behavior. moving to monitoring and post-incident actions.

nora (support): i'll attach timeline and interim mitigation to the open tickets and set expectation for a postmortem tomorrow.

oliver (pm): please include expected ETA for encoder memory fix and rollout plan in postmortem. customers asked for timeline.

kim (oncall): will keep the incident open for the next 2 hours, then transition to postmortem if stable. leaving instructions: do not remove suppression until both queue depth and restart rate are below thresholds for 30m.

tara (monitoring): created temporary dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/region-failover-encoder-burst ; will open dashboard PR #7765 to make panels permanent.

maya (sre): collected heap dump and uploaded to analysis bucket. pointer: s3://incidents/heapdumps/1945689999-encoder-1.hprof

chris (prod-eng): implemented quick fix to gate large-batch code path behind `--enable-batch-guard` flag; will test in canary cluster then rollout. PR: https://git.redwood/encoders/pull/345

rahul (oncall): marking mitigated at 1945690560. residual work: alert PRs from tara, autoscaler PR from maya, canary rollout from chris, and customer comms from nora/oliver.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated. created tracker: INC-2026-1142 `us-east encoder OOM causing regional failover`.

tara (monitoring): note on alert noise during the incident: we received 9 duplicate `encoder_pod_oom` alerts from different clusters. action: normalize alert dedup by cluster and add playbook: "on regional_traffic_shift, route duplicates into a single summary alert."

maya (sre): owners: chris -> encoder fix & canary, tara -> alert/dashboard PRs, kim -> runbook update and final verification, rahul -> customer postmortem draft.

kim (oncall): will validate PRs and sign off on suppression removal once stable. leaving thread open until 1945690600. reopen if anything regresses.

nora (support): final note: customers acknowledged mitigation and requested a 1-page timeline. i'll draft after postmortem is ready.

incident-bot: Reminder: run the postmortem template in GH within 48h and tag #incidents #eng-sre.

kim (oncall): last check 1945690600 1A metrics stable, closing incident thread from oncall side; shifting to action items.
